title: Retry After
summary: Turns a 429/503 into a clear wait: which limit was hit, when it resets, a countdown, and one automatic retry instead of impatient re-clicks.
description: Action button that, on 429/503, reads Retry-After (seconds or HTTP-date) and RateLimit headers, explains which limit was hit and when it resets, counts down, ignores impatient clicks and retries automatically with jitter while the user's input stays put.
catches: Retry-After as delay-seconds or an HTTP-date
IETF RateLimit / RateLimit-Policy fields and common X-RateLimit headers
Repeated clicks during the wait, swallowed with a gentle note
Automatic retry with jitter, capped by maxAutoRetries
Fallback backoff when the server gives no hint
limits: Client-side wait only; another tab or a direct request is not held back
RateLimit fields follow an IETF draft and vendor variants; unusual headers fall back to backoff
The countdown uses performance.now(), so it survives clock changes but not a page reload
a11y: While waiting the button stays focusable with aria-disabled (not disabled) and is described by the reason
aria-busy while the request is pending
Wait reason in a polite live region; the spam note is assertive; errors use role=alert
Label transition animation is skipped under reduced motion
server: Enforce the rate limit server-side and send Retry-After; the client wait only reduces wasted requests.

rules.note: Retry-After (HTTP-date or delay-seconds) confirmed in RFC 9110. RateLimit/RateLimit-Policy parsing follows an IETF draft and was not re-verified this round.
